title: First release
summary: A fast Git client for macOS written in Rust: the commit graph drawn on the GPU, tabs for every repository, GitHub pull requests in the sidebar and a stats view, all built from what git already knows.

features.title: GPU commit graph
features.body: The history is drawn on the GPU in a virtualized list, colourful lanes and ref chips included, smooth even past 100,000 commits.

features.title: Repository tabs and workspaces
features.body: Every repository in a tab, restored at launch, grouped in named workspaces. Hold ⌃ and press Tab to pick one among cards.

features.title: Pull requests in the sidebar
features.body: Each branch with a PR gets a #123 chip coloured by state with its CI result; a PRs tab lists the reviews you owe, drafts, stacks and recent merges.

features.title: Stats view
features.body: Top authors, reviewers, activity chart, weekday × hour heatmap and hot files, computed from commits only.

features.title: Stage, commit and push
features.body: Stage per file or per hunk, commit, amend, commit and push, with a syntax-highlighted diff and intra-line changes.

features.title: Checkout like Fork
features.body: Double-click a branch; with local changes a sheet offers to keep, stash and reapply, or discard them. The new HEAD shows at once.

features.title: Commit search
features.body: Search by message, author, branch, tag or SHA with matches highlighted in the graph.

features.title: Automatic fetch
features.body: Every 10 s for the focused repository, every 5 min for the others, with a pulsing dot on tabs whose remotes moved.
